trap-negation-contrast.evidence: table( pure-data block, 7 rows of skew SYT counts f^{lambda/[2,1]}. RECOMPUTED every row by counting linear extensions of the skew cell poset: [2,1]/[2,1]=empty->1; [3,1]/[2,1]=1 cell->1; [2,2]/[2,1]=1 cell->1; [3,1,1]/[2,1]={(1,3),(3,1)} incomparable->2; [3,2]/[2,1]={(1,3),(2,2)} incomparable->2; [3,2,1]/[2,1]={(1,3),(2,2),(3,1)} mutually incomparable->3!=6; [4,2,1]/[2,1]={(1,3),(1,4),(2,2),(3,1)} with only (1,3)<(1,4)->4!/2=12. All 7 rows correct. Independent invariants: [3,2]'=[2,2,1] confirms the stated conjugate pair; [3,2,1]'=[3,2,1] and [2,2]'=[2,2] confirm the stated self-conjugacy; dim S_[3,2,1]=16 is the largest S_6 irreducible, consistent with 'largest w_lambda'. Parent's '191 partitions at k=3..11' also checks: p(3)+...+p(11)=3+5+7+11+15+22+30+42+56=191.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: Two labelling notes (arithmetic is clean): (i) [2,2] is self-conjugate but is NOT a hook shape (hooks are (a,1^b)), so the cell 'Hook (self-conjugate baryon)' invites a misreading -- it appears to be a Bethe-Weizsaecker term name; (ii) the k=3 row names the BW terms 'Volume, Surface, Coulomb, Asymmetry, Exchange' where the standard semi-empirical fifth term is Pairing. Both inherited from the parent. The 4_1-is-the-unknot anomaly recorded on table1 has the same parent and applies here.
